meta.description: 20 cleaned logic problems (5 each: negation, conditional, quantifier, spatial), cleaned from the actual Week 1 '20 Questions' set per the Part C criteria: True/False relabeled to Entailed/Contradicted/Unknown, one core logical phenomenon per item where possible, no dependence on unstated world knowledge, and a formal/symbolic ground truth for every item.
meta.source: Week 1 '20 Questions' document (Negation / Conditionals / Quantifiers / Spatial Relations sections), items 1-20.
cleaning_changes: Items 8, 10, 14 were relabeled. Under classical entailment semantics these are fallacies (affirming the consequent, denying the antecedent, undistributed middle respectively): the premises neither entail nor contradict the query, so the correct label is Unknown. The original Week 1 answer key marked all three False, which conflates 'not validly derivable' with 'derivably false' -- exactly the ambiguity Part C's True/False -> Entailed/Contradicted/Unknown relabeling is meant to remove.

Items 18 and 19 implicitly relied on knowing that 'behind'/'in front of' and 'east of'/'west of' are converse relations -- unstated lexical world knowledge. Made each converse relation an explicit formal meaning-postulate premise (e.g. forall(X,Y, behind(X,Y) <-> front_of(Y,X))) so the ground truth is self-contained rather than depending on implicit semantics, per Part C.

All other items (1-7, 9, 11-13, 15-17, 20) were already single-phenomenon and free of external world-knowledge dependence; only their label was renamed (True->Entailed, False->Contradicted) and a formal representation was added.

items.label: contradicted

items.label: contradicted

premises_nl: Nina does not own a bicycle.
items.label: contradicted

items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Daniel did not lose the key.
items.label: contradicted

premises_nl: If Emma studies, she passes the exam.
Emma studies.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: If the alarm rings, Mia leaves the building.
The alarm rings.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: If Noah exercises, he feels tired.
Noah feels tired.
items.label: unknown
items.cleaning_note: Original Week 1 label was False. Affirming the consequent is a fallacy: tiredness could have another cause, so the premises don't determine whether Noah exercised. Correct label under Entailed/Contradicted/Unknown is Unknown.

premises_nl: If Ava takes the bus, she arrives before noon.
Ava does not arrive before noon.
items.label: contradicted

premises_nl: If Leo presses the button, the machine starts.
Leo does not press the button.
items.label: unknown
items.cleaning_note: Original Week 1 label was False. Denying the antecedent is a fallacy: the machine could start some other way, so the premises don't determine whether it starts. Correct label is Unknown.

premises_nl: All painters are artists.
Maria is a painter.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: No cats are reptiles.
Felix is a cat.
items.label: contradicted

premises_nl: All teachers are employees.
Some teachers are musicians.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Some students are athletes.
Some students are musicians.
items.label: unknown
items.cleaning_note: Original Week 1 label was False. This is the classic undistributed-middle fallacy: the athlete-students and musician-students need not overlap, so the premises neither entail nor contradict the query. Correct label is Unknown, not Contradicted.

premises_nl: No doctors are pilots.
Some doctors are writers.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: The apple is left of the book.
The book is left of the cup.
items.query_nl: The apple is left of the cup.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Mia is north of Noah.
Noah is north of Liam.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: The chair is behind the desk.
items.query_nl: The desk is in front of the chair.
premises_formal: forall(X, Y, behind(X, Y) <-> front_of(Y, X))
items.label: entailed
items.cleaning_note: Original item implicitly relied on knowing 'behind' and 'in front of' are converse relations, an unstated lexical fact. Added the converse relation as an explicit formal meaning-postulate premise so the item's ground truth is self-contained per Part C.

premises_nl: The park is east of the school.
The library is east of the park.
items.query_nl: The library is west of the school.
premises_formal: forall(X, Y, west_of(X, Y) <-> east_of(Y, X))
items.label: contradicted
items.cleaning_note: Same fix as spat_03: made the east_of/west_of converse relation an explicit formal premise rather than assumed world knowledge. Kept as a compound transitivity+converse item ('as much as possible' single-phenomenon, not absolute, per Part C) since it deliberately tests whether direction is tracked correctly across a chain and a converse together.

premises_nl: The red box is above the blue box.
The blue box is above the green box.
items.query_nl: The green box is above the red box.
items.label: contradicted
